name: doltlite
desc: SQLite fork with Git-style version control via prolly trees
why: SQLite with git-style versioning built on prolly trees, a strange and genuinely original database idea to explore.

brief.what_it_is: DoltLite is a fork of SQLite that replaces SQLite's B-tree storage engine with a content-addressed prolly tree, giving Git-style version control over a SQL database. The parser, planner and VDBE stay upstream-derived; below SQLite's btree.h seam, a single-file chunk store backs the prolly trees. Version control is exposed as dolt_* SQL functions and virtual tables such as dolt_commit, dolt_branch, dolt_merge, dolt_diff_<table> and dolt_log. It ships as a doltlite CLI shell, a doltlite-remotesrv sync server and a libdoltlite C library with bindings for Python, Ruby, Node, Rust, Go and other languages. Stock SQLite files are still opened on the original B-tree engine.
brief.why_it_exists: The README frames it as a way to bring Dolt's versioned, prolly-tree design to embedded, local-first use: DoltLite "can be embedded in any language enabling local-first use cases for Dolt." The linked blog post "Why DoltLite?" gives the longer rationale, which I did not fetch.
brief.how_it_works: Each database is one content-addressed chunk-store file rather than SQLite pages. Prolly trees are built from immutable nodes with rolling-hash boundaries, the same design the README says Dolt uses. Branches, commits, diffs and merges operate on those trees, and each connection selects its own branch.

brief.install_notes: No Homebrew-specific steps appear in the README. Options: a curl-piped install.sh for macOS arm64 and Linux (needs sudo); Debian/Ubuntu .deb packages for amd64 and arm64 (the example version lookup needs jq); a Windows zip containing doltlite.exe that you add to PATH; or building from source with cd build, ../configure, make. Language bindings are installed through each ecosystem's package manager (pip, gem, npm, composer, dotnet, cargo, go get, SwiftPM, Gradle). C embedding needs #include <doltlite.h> and linking libdoltlite.a -lpthread -lz. Nothing in the README mentions accounts or hardware.
brief.standout: It puts Git-style branches, merges, diffs and conflict resolution inside an ordinary embedded SQL database that is one file, instead of a separate server like Dolt. Merge conflicts exist only inside the transaction that produced them and never reach disk, and the built-in vec1 vector index is versioned and merges like the rest of the data.
brief.status: The README labels DoltLite Beta and links a 2026-08-31 beta announcement; it also states that storage format version 12 is frozen for the beta. The fetched README shows no release tag, release date or last-commit date, so I cannot confirm activity from this page alone. Maintenance status: unknown.
brief.caveats: Beta software. A write transaction may touch only one file-backed database. PRAGMA journal_mode reports wal and ignores changes. Non-integer primary keys are clustered and NOT NULL, and rowid is read-only for them. doltlite-remotesrv binds to localhost until TLS and authentication are configured. Vector PQ training needs at least 512 vectors. The README gives no license information, and I did not check the repository's license file. Windows is distributed as a zip rather than an installer.
quotes: A SQLite fork that replaces the B-tree storage engine with a content-addressed prolly tree, giving Git-like version control on a SQL database.
Each connection has its own branch; uncommitted work belongs to the branch.
Conflicts are never durable; they live only in the transaction that made them.
